entries.headline: Before /dev:run-slice: create the healthchecks.io check (period 5 minutes, grace 10 minutes, Telegram integration) and write its ping URL to kv/eso/prd/prometheus/prd/healthchecks
body: Rulings D1/F1: the dead-man's switch is a healthchecks.io check that Alertmanager pings at most every 5 minutes (P4). In healthchecks.io, create a check with period 5 minutes and grace 10 minutes, and route its notification to Telegram through healthchecks.io's own integration (@HealthchecksBot). A new check stays in 'new' state until its first ping, so creating it before the run notifies nobody. Then write its ping URL from stdin: `bao kv put kv/eso/prd/prometheus/prd/healthchecks ping_url=-` (docs/live-infra-access.md, 'Writing OpenBao secrets via bao kv put'). The test phase pushes PrometheusDeploy and Argo CD syncs it to prd straight away. Alertmanager's pod then mounts the Secret ESO materialises from this leaf.
entries.consequence: Without the leaf, Alertmanager's restarted pod waits on its missing Secret mount once the test phase pushes P4, and no alert reaches Telegram until the leaf exists.
entries.proposal: do it — one check in healthchecks.io and one bao kv put; the run's push of PrometheusDeploy depends on it.

entries.headline: Before /dev:run-slice: generate the filebeat reader's password and write it to kv/eso/prd/elasticsearch/prd/filebeat-reader
body: Settled ruling: the operator generates the read-only Elasticsearch user's password and writes it to OpenBao with one bao kv put. The setup Job takes it through ESO (P6), and the KubeCoder card (KC-124) reads the same leaf later. Write it from stdin, never as a positional argument: `bao kv put kv/eso/prd/elasticsearch/prd/filebeat-reader password=-`. prd's ESO already reads eso/prd/* (ansible/inventories/prd/group_vars/openbao.yml:99), so no policy change is needed.
entries.consequence: Without the leaf, the setup Job's pod waits on its missing Secret after the test phase's push, the reader is never created, and the runbook confirmation (P7, V10) cannot be made.
entries.proposal: do it — one bao kv put; the run's ElasticsearchDeploy push and the runbook confirmation depend on it.

entries.headline: NginxDeploy: https:// on a .home host without its own TLS server answers 200 with the Architecture validation service
body: Witnessed 2026-10-03 with curl: https://kibana.home/, https://prometheus.home/ and https://alertmanager.home/ each return HTTP 200 with the page titled 'Architecture validation service'. Their http:// URLs reach the right app (Kibana's /login redirect, Prometheus' /query, Alertmanager). NginxDeploy declares a default server for port 80 only (chart/files/conf.d/20-default_server.conf:4), so nginx gives an unmatched TLS name to whichever 443 server comes first, and a wrong scheme lands on an unrelated app instead of failing. docs/runbooks/argocd.md's Kibana route gives https://kibana.home today. P7 of this slice corrects that one URL. Other docs and other hosts were not surveyed.
entries.consequence: A reader or agent who follows an https:// .home link gets an unrelated page with a 200 status, not an error. An agent using curl can take it for the service answering.
entries.author: plan-writer, planning, round 3, slices/backlog/040_alerting_and_log_access/plan.md P7

entries.headline: Settle V02 after the operator's `ansible-playbook playbooks/site.yml --limit srviac`, …
body: V02 — "Whether DHCP answers at all: a DISCOVER from outside the pod network": a probe on srviac sends a relay-style DISCOVER to the DHCP service every few minutes and records the result through srviac's node-exporter. A critical alert fires when no OFFER comes back, and a warning fires when the result is stale or missing. The probe takes no lease. Evidence at planning: one DISCOVER from srviac with giaddr 10.1.0.45, sent from UDP 67, got an OFFER (10.1.1.80) after 3.018 s, from 10.1.0.29:85, and dnsmasq logged DHCPDISCOVER/DHCPOFFER for it (attachments/dhcp-probe.md).

`verification.json` marks V02 owed after: the operator's `ansible-playbook playbooks/site.yml --limit srviac`, which puts the probe on srviac. The run cannot take that action; settle the criterion once it has happened.
entries.consequence: V02 stays unproven until then; the test phase does not settle it.
entries.proposal: When that has happened, say so: the session settles V02 in verification.json.

entries.headline: Ansible dhcp_probe: --check skips the timer task on every run, so a dry run never shows the timer's enable/start or its drift
body: ansible/roles/dhcp_probe/tasks/main.yml:21-30 has `when: not ansible_check_mode` on the enable/start task. This is the microk8s watchdog.yml:43-45 precedent, and the P1 done-record states it. The first run's dry run previews only the file diffs. On a converged host where dhcp-probe.timer has been stopped or disabled, --check reports nothing, and the apply then reports changed=1.
entries.consequence: A dry run of srviac's play does not show the timer being enabled or a stopped timer being restarted. P3's staleness warning raises a stopped timer in production.
